done: BASE: main d5003f5, in worktree Concordance-V3-exact on branch exact-integers. One step, fix, holding the rule, the probe, the table, every fix and its tests; the step's note records the base measure first: the probe's findings and the table's claim reads at d5003f5, each listed. It ships through deploy/install.sh at an exact sha after green CI on the branch and on main, on the owner's standing word for V3 ships.

THE RULE: one reader of an integer from a spec, the rule mathematics._exact_integer keeps (mathematics.py:1926-1935): an int; a float only when finite and whole; a text only when int() reads it whole; a bool never; anything else refused. It moves to one shared place under src/concordance/verifiers/ that mathematics and every fixed site import, and mathematics reads exactly as before. A refused value is never dropped and never read as a pass. Where the value is a claimed result, the check reads as it reads any wrong claim (the step MISMATCH, the derivation BROKEN). Where the check's own question is whether the value is valid, as atomic.quantum_numbers asks of a set, the value reads invalid and the check compares that with the claim. Where the value is an input the check computes from, the step reads ERROR with the malformed-number sentence mathematics already uses. Each fixed site's entry in the step's note says which of the three it is.

THE PROBE: a tool, a mode of an existing tool where one fits (tools/mc_fuzz.py or tools/fault_sweep.py) or else tools/integer_probe.py, reads data/check_goldens.jsonl. For each check whose true spec reads HOLDS with no fault, it replaces each integer leaf of that spec (an int, never a bool, at any depth), one at a time, by the leaf plus 0.5, and, where the leaf is 0 or 1, also by the bool of the same truth. A finding is a variant whose derivation reads HOLDS. A leaf may be named in tests/integer_fields.json as real-valued, with the check, the leaf's path, why a fraction is a meaningful value there, and one input with a fraction that a test runs and that reads as the check should; a named leaf's fraction variant is not a finding, and its bool variant always is. The probe finds a fraction dropped by any means (int, round, floor, floor division), anywhere on the check's path. It runs in the suite in its own child process with CONCORDANCE_MEMO=0, is deterministic, writes nothing into data/, states its run count and time in the step's note, and must find 0. At the base its findings must include combinatorics.permutations' claimed_permutations, periodic_table.element's claimed_atomic_number and atomic.quantum_numbers' n.

THE TABLE: tests/integer_reads.json lists every int() call left in src/concordance/verifiers/*.py after the fix, found by parsing each file (a call whose function is the name int), keyed by file, enclosing function, and the call's source text with its occurrence number, never by line. Each entry names where its argument comes from, as one of: a length or count the code computed; a result of the code's own arithmetic or a library's (such as a sympy Integer); text the code matched as digits only, with the pattern named; a value already read by THE RULE. No entry reads a spec or claim value directly. A test fails on any int() call not in the table and on any entry with no call. Checks with no true spec in check_goldens.jsonl, and fields a true spec does not carry, are held by THE TABLE, not THE PROBE.

TESTS, with no fault, each red at the base: P(5,2) claimed 20.9 reads as a wrong claim, while 20 reads HOLDS and 21 reads as a wrong claim as today. Iron claimed atomic number 26.5 or 'twenty-seven', and hydrogen claimed true, read as a wrong claim; iron 26 and '26' read HOLDS and 27 as today; the one reading that moves is named, the text '26.0', which reads HOLDS today only because the claim is dropped and reads as a wrong claim after. A quantum-number set with n 2.7, with m_l 0.5, or with m_l true, claimed valid, reads as a wrong claim, and n 2, l 1, m_l 0, m_s 0.5 claimed valid still reads HOLDS (m_s is named real-valued). Each further site the probe or the table finds has a test with the input that read HOLDS at the base.

UNCHANGED: with no fault the benchmark stays 1796 of 1796 with 0 false positives and 0 false negatives and every case reads as before; tools/check.py GATE PASS; tools/vocab_gate.py 0 hits; the full suite passes against the baseline; the moat holds; no public number drawn from the benchmark changes. A golden whose own integer leaf THE RULE refuses is reported in the step's note as a finding of this run, never edited to pass.

text: checker-98, plan review, measured on a scratch export of d5003f5 through verify_derivation, in process, CONCORDANCE_MEMO=0, no fault; nothing run in a checkout, nothing live. (1) data/check_goldens.jsonl: 428 checks, all 428 true specs read HOLDS, 1168 integer leaves (143 of them 0 or 1, 35 negative). (2) THE PROBE exactly as written (leaf+0.5, and the bool for 0/1 leaves): 1739 runs, 14.6 s, 939 findings on 207 checks, 800 fraction and 139 bool. The three it must find at the base are there: combinatorics.permutations claimed_permutations 20, periodic_table.element claimed_atomic_number 6, atomic.quantum_numbers n 3. Of the 800 fraction findings, 286 (137 distinct spec and leaf) drop the fraction (leaf+1 reads not HOLDS); 341 (128 distinct) sit inside a tolerance (leaf+1 also HOLDS); 173 (111 distinct) do not move the verdict at all (10*leaf+7 still HOLDS). Of the 139 bool findings, 71 sit at leaves whose fraction variant does not read HOLDS (real-valued float reads, e.g. geography lat1 0, LIN_VERIFY matrix entries 1, PROB_VERIFY normal_sigma 1, ACOUS_VERIFY v_source_mps 0), and 3 at leaves no check of that spec reads: condensed_matter.fermi_energy diff_order, finance.accounting_identity pv_periods, photonics.ring_resonator_fsr order (997, or the text zzz-not-a-number, there still reads HOLDS). (3) leaf+0.25 and leaf-0.25 reach 66 leaves leaf+0.5 misses; among them architecture.occupant_load claimed_occupant_count 109: 109.4 and 108.6 read HOLDS, 109.5 reads BROKEN (int(round(c)), half to even); history_chronology.year_arithmetic from_year -44: -44.3 HOLDS, -43.5 BROKEN. (4) TESTS at the base: P(5,2) claimed 20.9 HOLDS, 20 HOLDS, 21 BROKEN, '20.0' SYSTEM_ERROR; iron claimed 26.5, 'twenty-seven', '26.0', 26, '26' HOLDS, 27 BROKEN; hydrogen claimed true HOLDS; n 2.7, m_l 0.5, m_l true (l 1) claimed valid HOLDS; n 2 l 1 m_l 0 m_s 0.5 claimed valid HOLDS. Claimed invalid: n 2.7 reads BROKEN, n 'abc' and n null read SYSTEM_ERROR. (5) mathematics.verify_number_theory, 5! claimed: 120.5 MISMATCH; true, '120.0' and 'one hundred twenty' ERROR (malformed number-theory input), read by _claimed_integer at mathematics.py:1945-1952. (6) An AST pass finds 224 int() calls in 47 verifier files, about 100 of them in 28 files reading a spec value directly or through float, round, abs or str. (7) All 1796 benchmark cases with each verifier module's int replaced by a logging twin (mathematics and statistics left plain; every verdict equal to the plain run): no true case passes a bool or a fractional spec value to int(); the fractional calls in true cases are the code's own arithmetic (elliptic_curves _primes and verify_l_value, number_theory schoenfeld, nicolas, _zeros_in_strip).

findings: THE PROBE (what a finding is; 'must find 0' cannot hold as written): measured at d5003f5 (note above), the probe as written reads 939 findings on 207 of the 428 checks, 800 fraction and 139 bool, and only 286 of the 800 (137 distinct spec and leaf) drop a fraction. 341 (128 distinct) are real-valued leaves inside a tolerance (leaf+1 also reads HOLDS, e.g. ACOUS_VERIFY speed_medium_mps 343), and 173 (111 distinct) do not move the verdict at all (10*leaf+7 still reads HOLDS), so zeroing the probe means about 240 integer_fields.json entries, each with a test, and for an unread leaf 'why a fraction is a meaningful value there' has no true answer. The bool rule cannot reach 0: 3 bool findings sit at leaves no check of that spec reads (condensed_matter.fermi_energy diff_order, finance.accounting_identity pv_periods, photonics.ring_resonator_fsr order; 997 or a non-number text there still reads HOLDS), so no verifier change moves them, and goldens are never edited to pass. 71 more sit at real-valued float() reads whose fraction is honoured (geography lat1/lon1 0, LIN_VERIFY matrix entries 1, PROB_VERIFY normal_mu 0 and normal_sigma 1, ACOUS_VERIFY v_source_mps 0), which neither THE RULE (an integer reader) nor THE TABLE (int() calls) covers. Answer: count a fraction finding only when an integer step of the same leaf (leaf+1 and leaf-1) reads not HOLDS, and treat a leaf whose far value still reads HOLDS as unread, so it makes no finding. Then either count a bool finding only where an integer step moves the verdict, or give THE RULE a real-number reader (never a bool) with its three readings and a table of its float() reads. State the base counts that result.

THE PROBE with THE TABLE (leaf+0.5 misses round and negative int; 'directly' lets a wrapped claim through): 'finds a fraction dropped by any means (int, round, floor, floor division)' is false for +0.5, because round() rounds half to even and int() truncates toward zero. Measured at the base: architecture.occupant_load claimed_occupant_count, golden 109: 109.4 and 108.6 read HOLDS, while 109.5 reads BROKEN (round(109.5) = 110), so the probe misses int(round(c)) at architecture.py:99-106. history_chronology.year_arithmetic from_year -44: -44.3 reads HOLDS, -43.5 reads BROKEN. leaf+0.25 and leaf-0.25 together reach 66 leaves +0.5 misses. THE TABLE forbids only an entry that reads a spec value 'directly', so int(round(c)) there and int(float(claimed)) at wordcraft.py:219, 265, 293, 298, 319, 358 and 581 can be labelled 'a result of the code's own arithmetic or a library's', and architecture's claim site then passes both nets. Answer: use leaf+0.25 and leaf-0.25 (with the integer-step control above). Say that an int() whose argument comes from a spec value through any call (round, float, abs, str) reads that value, and have the table's test check this by walking each enclosing function, not by trusting the label.

THE RULE (a claimed result) against mathematics.py:1945-1952: mathematics does not read claims with _exact_integer. It reads them with _claimed_integer, where a finite fraction stands as written and reads MISMATCH, and a bool or a text int() refuses reads ERROR, 'malformed number-theory input'. Measured at the base, mathematics.verify_number_theory 5! claimed 120.5 reads MISMATCH; claimed true, '120.0' and 'one hundred twenty' read ERROR. TESTS want iron 'twenty-seven', hydrogen true and '26.0' to read as wrong claims (BROKEN), while 'mathematics reads exactly as before'. That gives the same malformed claim two readings under 'one reader'. The plan also names no reading that moves from ERROR to BROKEN at claim sites where int()'s refusal reads ERROR today: P(5,2) claimed '20.0' reads SYSTEM_ERROR at the base. Answer: say whether the fixed claim sites take _claimed_integer's reading (then 'twenty-seven', true and '26.0' read SYSTEM_ERROR, and TESTS change) or why they differ from mathematics. Name every reading that moves, with a test.

THE RULE (the validity reading) against its own 'a refused value is never dropped and never read as a pass': for atomic.quantum_numbers, a refused value claimed invalid compares invalid with invalid and reads CONFIRMED, which is a pass. Measured at the base with l 1, m_l 0, m_s 0.5: n 2.7 claimed invalid reads BROKEN, and n 'abc' and n null claimed invalid read SYSTEM_ERROR. Under the validity reading all three read HOLDS, new passes that TESTS do not name. Answer: say which holds. Either these read HOLDS, named as readings that move to HOLDS with a test each, or a refused value claimed invalid reads ERROR, with that test.

BASE (one step) against HARNESS 'Smallest' and the goal's count: the goal says about thirty sites, but an AST pass at d5003f5 finds about 100 of the 224 int() calls, in 28 verifier files, reading a spec value directly or through float, round, abs or str. The probe reads 939 findings at the base. One step holding the rule, the probe, the table, every fix and a test per site cannot be the smallest step, and the live exposure (the four HOLDS readings in the goal) waits on all of it, through a step that blocks after three failed verdicts. Answer: a first step with the shared reader, the three named sites and the TESTS cases, shipped first; then further steps by file group; and the probe's 0 and the table's test in the last step, each red at its own base.

OTHER RUNS: run 2026-11-11-errors-fail-closed's step one, committed at 970f173 on its branch and not on main, pins its sweep's findings and reach by statement position in functions this run rewrites. Its tests/fault_sweep_known.json holds findings at verifiers.atomic:verify_quantum_numbers:body[6].body[0].handlers[0] and body[7].body[0].handlers[0]. Its tests/fault_sweep_reach.json holds verify_quantum_numbers:body[2], combinatorics verify_permutations:body[3].body[0] and others. test_the_default_sweep_makes_exactly_the_known_findings requires exactly that list. Also, tools/fault_sweep.py, offered here as a home for the probe, is not at d5003f5 (it exists only in 970f173), so a mode there would add the file on this branch and collide with that run. Answer: say how that run's step one reaches the new main (re-measured known and reach files with its checker gate re-run, per the-rebase-note-maps-by-patch-id) and drop fault_sweep.py as a home.

LIVE: 'the service's restart count is unchanged across the live check' cannot be read through a public URL, and a checker never sshes. checker-90 (run 2026-11-04-gcd-lcm-order, line 193) and checker-82 (run 2026-11-06-killable-cells, line 34) recorded that NRestarts and MainPID cannot be read publicly. done: BASE: main d5003f5, in worktree Concordance-V3-exact on branch exact-integers. Three steps, one at a time. Step measure adds the probe, the walk, their known lists and their tests, and changes nothing under src/. Step fix-a adds THE RULE's one shared module and closes every finding in combinatorics.py, periodic_table.py, atomic.py, number_theory.py, wordcraft.py and operations_research.py, with TESTS. Step fix-b closes every other finding and empties both known lists. Each known list may only shrink, and each fix step removes exactly its own files' entries. The run ships through deploy/install.sh at an exact sha after green CI on the branch and on main, on the owner's standing word for V3 ships.

THE RULE: mathematics' two readers, as they read today (mathematics.py:1926-1952), move to one shared module under src/concordance/verifiers/ that mathematics and every fixed site import; mathematics reads exactly as before, its own refusal sentence included. An input reads by _exact_integer: an int, a finite whole float, or a text int() reads whole; anything else (a fraction, a bool, other text, null) reads malformed, the step ERROR and the derivation SYSTEM_ERROR. A claimed result reads by _claimed_integer: a number with a fraction, or a text whose float has one, stands as written, so the check reads it as a wrong claim, the step MISMATCH and the derivation BROKEN; a whole number reads as its integer; anything else reads malformed. Where the check's own question is whether a value is valid, as atomic.quantum_numbers asks of a set, a number with a fraction reads invalid and the check compares that with the claim, and anything else reads malformed. A refused value is never dropped and never read as the integer it is not. The shared reader's refusal names the field and says the value is not a whole number, in words that fit any domain; each fixed site says which of the three readings it uses.

THE PROBE: tools/integer_probe.py, new (tools/fault_sweep.py is not at the base), run in its own child process with CONCORDANCE_MEMO=0. For each check whose true spec in data/check_goldens.jsonl reads HOLDS with no fault, it varies each integer leaf (an int, never a bool, at any depth), one at a time, to v+0.25 and v-0.25, and a leaf of 0 or 1 also to the bool of the same truth. It watches the calls that can drop a fraction or take a bool for an integer, int(), round() with one argument (found by parsing the file), math.floor, math.ceil and math.trunc, called from a file under src/concordance/verifiers/, with Python's sys.monitoring CALL events. A finding is such a call that receives a bool or a finite float with a fraction, and either receives the injected value itself or sits at a site that is not lossy in the clean run of the same case. It is keyed by check, leaf path, variant and site, the site written as file, enclosing function and the call's source text with its occurrence number, never a line. A finding counts whatever the variant's verdict; the verdict is recorded beside it. A leaf no check reads makes no call and so no finding. A call that floors or rounds a real value on purpose, as the check's own definition, is named in tests/integer_fields.json with its site, why, and a test whose fractional input reads as the check should; its findings are not counted. At the base its findings are its known list, tests/integer_probe_known.json, and must include combinatorics.permutations' claimed_permutations, perm_n and perm_k, periodic_table.element's claimed_atomic_number and atomic.quantum_numbers' n. It is deterministic, writes nothing into data/, and the step's note states its run count and time.

THE WALK: a test parses each file under src/concordance/verifiers/ and follows each function's assignments from its parameters. A value is marked when it is a parameter, or computed from a marked value by attribute, subscript, arithmetic, or a call with a marked argument, including through unpacking, a for loop's target, and a comprehension or generator's target (taken as part of the function that holds it); a value is unmarked when it comes from THE RULE's readers, len(), a comparison, or a literal. A finding is an int(), one-argument round(), math.floor, math.ceil or math.trunc call whose argument is marked, unless its site is named in tests/integer_fields.json. At the base its findings are its known list, tests/integer_walk_known.json, keyed as THE PROBE keys sites, and they must include every site THE PROBE finds there, so the two measures check each other. THE WALK holds what THE PROBE cannot reach: checks with no true spec in check_goldens.jsonl and fields a true spec does not carry. A test of the walk itself shows that each kind of marking and unmarking is followed, and that an int() of a parameter added to a scratch copy is found.

TESTS, with no fault, each red at the base where its reading moves (base readings measured by the lead with tests_base.py). P(5,2): claimed 20.9 moves from HOLDS to BROKEN; true moves from BROKEN to SYSTEM_ERROR; P(5.5,2) and P(5,2.5) claimed 20 move from HOLDS to SYSTEM_ERROR; 20, 20.0 and '20' read HOLDS, 21 BROKEN and '20.0' SYSTEM_ERROR, as today. Iron's atomic number: claimed 26.5 moves from HOLDS to BROKEN; 'twenty-seven' and '26.0' move from HOLDS to SYSTEM_ERROR; hydrogen claimed true moves from HOLDS to SYSTEM_ERROR; 26, 26.0 and '26' read HOLDS, hydrogen 1 HOLDS and iron 27 BROKEN, as today. A quantum-number set (n 2, l 1, m_l 0, m_s 0.5 unless named): n 2.7 or m_l 0.5 claimed valid moves from HOLDS to BROKEN, and claimed invalid moves from BROKEN to HOLDS, since a quantum number with a fraction is invalid; m_l true claimed valid moves from HOLDS to SYSTEM_ERROR and claimed invalid from BROKEN to SYSTEM_ERROR; the set as given claimed valid, and n '2' claimed valid, read HOLDS, and n 'abc' or null claimed invalid read SYSTEM_ERROR, as today. Each further site closed has a test with an input that reached a lossy call at the base. This run supersedes plan nine of run 2026-11-11-errors-fail-closed for periodic_table.py:247-252: where that plan read 'twenty-seven', true and '26.0' as wrong claims, this run reads them malformed, as mathematics reads such claims today.

A golden whose own integer leaf THE RULE refuses is reported in the step's note as a finding of this run, never edited to pass.

A finding is such a call that receives a bool or a finite float with a fraction, and either receives the injected value itself or sits at a site that is not lossy in the clean run of the same case. It is keyed by check, leaf path, variant and site, the site written as file, enclosing function and the call's source text with its occurrence number, never a line. A finding counts whatever the variant's verdict; the verdict is recorded beside it. A leaf no check reads makes no call and so no finding. A call that floors or rounds a real value on purpose, as the check's own definition, is named in tests/integer_fields.json with its site, why, and a test whose fractional input reads as the check should; its findings are not counted. No site the probe finds receiving an injected value itself may be named there; such a site reads through THE RULE. With that it is deterministic: two runs give the same findings. It writes nothing into data/, and the step's note states its run count and time. sys.monitoring needs Python 3.12, so its test skips with that reason below 3.12 (the package allows 3.10; CI runs 3.12 and the box 3.14).

THE WALK: a test parses each file under src/concordance/verifiers/ and follows each function's assignments from its parameters. A value is marked when it is a parameter, or computed from a marked value by attribute, subscript, arithmetic, or a call with a marked argument, including through unpacking, a for loop's target, and a comprehension or generator's target (taken as part of the function that holds it); a value is unmarked when it comes from THE RULE's readers, len(), a comparison, or a literal. A finding is an int(), one-argument round(), math.floor, math.ceil or math.trunc call whose argument is marked, unless its site is named in tests/integer_fields.json, or is the conversion inside THE RULE's two shared readers themselves, which convert only a value they have already found whole. At the base its findings are its known list, tests/integer_walk_known.json, keyed as THE PROBE keys sites, and they must include every site THE PROBE finds there, so the two measures check each other. THE WALK holds what THE PROBE cannot reach: checks with no true spec in check_goldens.jsonl and fields a true spec does not carry. Python 3.12.10, in the lead's venv (sympy 1.14.0, numpy 2.5.4, scipy 1.18.1, mpmath 1.3.0, tzdata), on a scratch copy of this content that is no git checkout: the two test files read 66 passed and 2 skipped in 40.70 s (the skips are the two shrink checks, with no git revision). The probe run there on its own gave 2907 reads in 11.2 s and the same 632 findings (key, how and verdict) as tests/integer_probe_known.json and as the 3.14 runs. The shrink checks, in a scratch git repository whose HEAD holds both lists: unchanged lists, 2 passed; one entry added to each list, 2 failed, each naming the added entry; the probe's entry removed, and the walk's added site still present, 1 failed; that site removed too, 2 passed. In CI's checkout (actions/checkout@v4 at depth 1, HEAD the commit under test) they compare a list with itself and pass without checking anything. On the box's tree, which is no git checkout, they skip. So growth is caught by the gate, not by CI.
